argument_summary: The admissible record supports only a narrow certification theory. Aggregate readiness passed, there were no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and the rollout is staged at 5% with a rollback switch, which supports monitored deployment. At the same time, the Spanish-language billing-support weakness remains exposed in the initial cohort, and the current risk-acceptance draft is neither approved nor specific to that exposure. Under the stated policy, the defensible audit position is not clean present-tense compliance based on rollout controls alone, but certification conditioned on explicit pre-launch model-card disclosure of that exposed limitation.
claims_about_business_cost: No claim is made that business cost changes the policy result. The relevant point is narrower: if the packet is framed as caveated certification tied to explicit disclosure, escalation is not necessary on the current record because the remaining issue can be handled through that bounded compliance condition rather than by treating rollout controls alone as sufficient.
claims_about_policy: The policy text is specific: rollout controls and monitoring do not remove disclosure duties when the affected use case remains exposed. Because the Spanish-language billing-support segment remains eligible in the 5% rollout and there is no approved risk acceptance covering that exposure, the only supportable compliance path in this record is explicit pre-launch disclosure of the limitation. Public governance sources on monitoring and model-card content help explain why staged rollout plus disclosure is a coherent governance approach, but they do not override the internal policy predicate.
concessions: The current record does not support treating certification as unqualified compliance today.
The risk-acceptance draft cannot be relied on because it is unapproved and does not mention the Spanish-language billing-support exposure.
Rollout staging, monitoring, and rollback support risk management but do not satisfy the disclosure requirement by themselves.
If explicit pre-launch disclosure is not actually completed, the certification claim is not adequately supported under the stated policy.
